evidence:
Source-level Pass for the isolation controls specified by the shipped profile; no claim of adversarial runtime certification. Authority: actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks sheet row 47 (check 46): "The agent can't read the criteria it's graded on or influence the reward ... grading is isolated in the verifier"; Internal Quality Checks row 47 supplies the same interpretation. Frozen rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:184-185 requires no criteria, judge client, RewardKit or readable rubric in the agent image. The staged contract:62-74, 98-109 and 160-164 supplies the separate verifier, sanitized unprivileged app launch and protected scoring/restart responsibilities. Relevant deterministic workbook rows 9, 11, 14, 19, 34 and 36 were read, alongside deterministic-checks.md:40, 46, 58-62. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md sections Specific lessons and Runtime and model evidence were applied: public instructions and runtime evidence remain distinct, and the golden does not establish a full judge run.

Builder boundary: task/task.toml:2 declares only /app and /assets as artifacts; :26-35 declares environment_mode = "separate" and puts the expected ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} placeholder exclusively in verifier.env. There is no literal live key in that block. task/environment/Dockerfile:9-15 installs Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1 and copies only "instructions/ /instructions/" and "assets/ /assets/". No judge client, RewardKit, tests or solution copy is present. Every builder-visible note and seed asset was read; their text is ordinary public product/runtime requirements. A read-only scan of all 32 instruction/environment/solution files, including compiled JS/CSS, checked the 73 criterion identifiers parsed from all five judge TOMLs, grading-path/key names, and provider-secret/private-key shapes; no matches were found. This is bounded source evidence, not a claim that regexes prove absence of all possible secrets. No actual secret was encountered or printed.

Verifier and submitted-app boundary: task/tests/Dockerfile:16-31 installs judge tooling only in the verifier image; :43-44 copies grading files to /tests and runs "chmod -R go-rwx /tests". task/tests/test.sh:3 uses "umask 077"; :10-12 creates/chmods the reward log directory to 700 and reapplies /tests protection. :72-83 rejects escaping /app symlinks; :85-95 makes app files usable and owned by UID/GID 65534 without exposing /tests. Both the initial launch (:104-111) and generated restart launch (:160-167) use "env -i", an explicit PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT/DB_PATH list, and "setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups". Thus the verifier authentication environment is not propagated to either app launch. The restart helper is under the protected log directory (:127, :190-193), and tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:25-40 invokes that fixed helper with only a safe PATH. All five judge TOMLs use stdio MCP; the functional judge alone references /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py with $APP_RESTART_HELPER, not an app-selected helper. The app can write its own app/database area; grading output remains in the protected log directory. tests/test.sh:203-227 invokes RewardKit on /tests/gates and /tests/scored and then the fixed /tests/tools/score.py. score.py:10 resolves the fixed protected scoring.toml; :35-38 reads verifier suite results, and :59-65 writes reward files there. It does not accept a submitted app's claimed reward as its source. solution/solve.sh:4-26 only installs solution/app into /app. The golden server serves the starters and public subdirectories (solution/app/server.js:100-103), rather than exposing the verifier tree.

Counterexample review: a conforming app may read its own public bundle and persist through DB_PATH; those paths remain available under test.sh:85-111, so those legitimate reads/writes must not be mistaken for rubric or reward access. A deliberately broken/malicious submission could try fs.readFileSync('/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml'), read process.env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or write /logs/verifier/reward.txt. Source tracing finds a separate barrier for each attempt: /tests traversal/read permissions, environment scrubbing, and a non-writable/non-traversable reward directory. Repeating the attempt after restart does not bypass the source controls because the restart launch repeats the same UID and environment restrictions. These are adversarial source traces, not executed attacks; no concrete successful false-pass or false-fail witness was found.

Binding and inherited-policy check: all 50 task and 34 rules manifest entries were rehashed with zero missing/mismatched files against qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/manifest.json, whose input_sha256 is a6a5219e9c5aa5e19c2b30acb01ca3a1719938a02ea09674cd18e08987bf43a9. environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to their frozen template copies. Public network mode and judge isolated=false are expected profile settings, not isolation findings by themselves.

Run evidence and limit: golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json identifies direct pinned Playwright, paid_provider=false and oracle_score_claimed=false. Every recorded actual_app_files and driver_sha256 entry, plus the functional TOML and prompt hashes, was independently compared with the actual current files and matched. The executed drivers/launch_workflow.py:31-38 assigns UID/GID 65534 and supplies only PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/DB_PATH/PORT. Its :58-73 extracts the actual canonical restart helper and calls the real restart MCP; RESULTS.json restart records success with PID 16 changing to 335. This gives partial runtime support for normal unprivileged launch/restart, not evidence that an adversarial app attempted and was denied rubric reads, parent-process credential reads, or reward writes. The driver does not execute the full configured RewardKit judge, and its observed 98.03-second product workflow is not judge timing. No new Docker run, paid call, network request, or task edit was performed. A production-runtime isolation proof would need a harmless sentinel credential and explicit denied-access probes under both original and restarted app processes; full configured judge/Oracle/target-model measurements remain outside this row's source-level pass and unmeasured.
